source: Transcribed from the Chroma 63200A Series High Power Electronic Load Operation & Programming Manual. The manual marks each command Channel-Specific or Global; channel-specific ones act on whichever channel CHANnel has selected. This is the 63200A command set — the modular 63600 series and the AC loads of the 63800 series are separate manuals and are not covered here. Rebuilt from the guide in August 2026. pdftotext floats this manual’s value column a row against its labels — the heading carries the Type value and the Type line the description — and reading the content by shape rather than by label recovered the commands that skew had been hiding. Two malformed entries are gone: “SYSTem:ERRor?.” and a CONFigure:AUTO:ON that had swallowed prose into its parameters. The guide misprints “[ADVance]:SINE:IAC?” with the colon outside the bracket and heads one entry “[ADVance:]OCP: LATCh” with a stray space; the first is corrected by the typos map and the second mended at parse, both deliberately. Query Syntax 1 and 2 give two spellings for the PROGram:DATA queries; the catalog keeps the first.

commands.description: The *CLS command executes the following actions: Clear these registers <1> Channel Status Event registers for all channels <2> Channel Summary Event register <3> Questionable Status Event register <4> Standard Event Status Event register <5> Operation Status Event register Clear the Error Queue If "Clear Status Command" immediately follows a program message terminator (<nl>), the "Output Queue" and the MAV bit are also cleared.

This command sets the condition of the Standard Event Status Enable register to determine which event (see *ESR?) is allowed to set the ESB (Event Summary Bit) for the Status Byte register. A "1" in the bit position enables the corresponding event. All of the events that enabled by Standard Event Status register are logically ORed to cause the Status Byte register ESB (bit 5) to be set. See descriptions of these three registers in Chapter 5.

A "1" in the bit position enables the corresponding event. All of the events that enabled by Standard Event Status register are logically ORed to cause the Status Byte register ESB (bit 5) to be set. This query reads the Standard Event Status register, which will be cleared after reading. See Chapter 5 for detailed explanation. Standard Event Status Event Register Bit Position 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0 Condition PON 0 CME EXE DDE QYE 0 OPC Bit Weight 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1

This command causes the interface to set the OPC bit (bit 0) of the Standard Event Status register when the Electronic Load has completed all pending operations.
This query returns an ASCII "1" when all pending operations are completed.
This command restores the electronic load to a state that was previously stored in memory with the *SAV command to the specified location (see *SAV).
This command forces an ABORt, *CLS, LOAD=PROT=CLE command and sets the parameters to factory default.
This command stores the present state of the single electronic load and all channel states of multiple loads in a specified memory location.

This command sets the condition of the Service Request Enable register to determine which event of the Status Byte register (see *STB) is allowed to set the MSS (Master Status Summary) bit. A "1" in the bit position is logically ORed to cause the Status Byte register Bit 6 (the Master Summary Status Bit) to be set. See details regarding the Status Byte register in Chapter 5. Setting Syntax *SRE<space><NR1>

This command sets the condition of the Service Request Enable register to determine which event of the Status Byte register (see *STB) is allowed to set the MSS (Master Status Summary) bit. A "1" in the bit position is logically ORed to cause the Status Byte register Bit 6 (the Master Summary Status Bit) to be set. See details regarding the Status Byte register in Chapter 5. Setting Syntax *SRE<space><NR1>

This query reads the Status Byte register. Note that the MSS (Master Summary Status) bit instead of RQS bit is returned in Bit 6. This bit indicates if the electronic load has at least one reason for requesting service. *STB? does not clear the Status Byte register, which is cleared only when subsequent action has cleared all its set bits. Refer to Chapter 5 for more information about this register. Status Byte Register Bit Position 7 6 5 4 3 2 10 Condition 0 MSS ESB MAV QUES CSUM 0 0 Bit Weight 128 64 32 16 8 4 21
